questions.question: A pharmaceutical company accidentally included a mildly poisonous substance in a popular over-the-counter drug. As a result, many users got sick and the company was faced with a lawsuit. Which of the following torts was most likely cited as a reason for the lawsuit:
questions.explanation: Negligence. Negligence is conduct that drops below a reasonable standard of care and causes harm to another person or persons. When a pharmaceutical company accidentally includes a poisonous substance in a drug, it is an example of negligence, not invasion of privacy, defamation, or strict liability. The company did not invade its consumers' privacy or harm its users' reputations (defamation). The company would not likely be held in strict liability because strict liability implies that the tortfeasor (the company) was engaged in an inherently dangerous activity. Making and selling over-the-counter drugs is not generally an inherently dangerous activity to the public.
questions.source: The Business Professor. (2016, July). Tort law. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://thebusinessprofessor.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/Topic-9-Tort-Law.pdf

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the basic torts relating to business enterprises

questions.question: Merchants that export fruits and vegetables to the country of Uzoo are required to pay a tax to the Uzoo government. This tax is known as a(n)
questions.explanation: Tariff. Tariffs are taxes on imported goods. When an imported product enters a country that requires a tariff, the merchant will pay a certain percentage of the product's value directly to the government. Many countries collect tariffs on imported products to protect domestic manufacturers. Tariffs, or import taxes, are not called export taxes, restrictions, or domestic fees.
questions.source: The Levin Institute. (2016). Import restrictions. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.globalization101.org/import-restrictions/

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of import/export law

questions.question: Alicia's Pizzas is a national frozen pizza brand. After being produced and frozen, Alicia's Pizzas are sold to a wholesaler, which then sells the pizzas to a retailer such as a supermarket. The supermarket then sells the pizzas to final consumers. This example demonstrates
questions.explanation: Indirect distribution. Indirect distribution is a channel of distribution in which goods and services move from the producer to intermediaries and then to consumers or industrial users. In other words, companies use “middlemen” to get their products into as many hands as possible while minimizing overall risks and expenses. Direct distribution, on the other hand, is a channel of distribution in which goods and services move directly from the producer to the consumer or industrial user. Alicia's Pizzas are not distributed using direct distribution since they are sold to a wholesaler and then to a retailer before they reach final consumers. Supply chain management involves supervising the complete process of getting products into the marketplace. Ideal market exposure is the concept of ensuring that a product is available to the target market without overexposing the product. Supply chain management and idea market exposure are not demonstrated in this example.
questions.source: LAP-CM-002—Chart Your Channels (Channel Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of channel management

questions.question: On her way home from work, Cara stops at a produce stand and buys a bag of fresh tomatoes from a local farmer. In this situation, Cara is the __________ and the farmer is the __________.
questions.explanation: Ultimate consumer; producer. An ultimate consumer is anyone who personally uses a good or service to satisfy her/his own needs or wants. In this example, Cara is the ultimate consumer; she is the final stop for the farmer's tomatoes. The farmer is the producer, because s/he grew the tomatoes that Cara purchased. In this example, there is no intermediary or retailer because Cara purchased the tomatoes directly from the producer.
questions.source: LAP-CM-003—Channel It (Channels of Distribution)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of channels of distribution

questions.question: A raw materials supplier recently implemented order tracking technology so that the company's customers know when their materials will arrive. This is an example of how technology in channel management can
questions.explanation: Improve customer service. Technology such as order tracking can help improve customer service among channel members by providing easier access to helpful information. When implemented correctly, channel management technologies can also improve efficiency, decrease overall expenses, and decrease delivery lead times within a distribution channel.
questions.source: Ingram, D. (2017, November 21). Channel management techniques. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/channel-management-techniques-3072.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain legal considerations in channel management

questions.question: Andrea recently got a great deal on an expensive camera—instead of paying $500 for the camera, she only paid $150. However, after opening the package, Andrea realized that the camera didn't come with an instruction manual or warranty information. If the camera breaks, she'll be out of luck. This is most likely an example of which of the following ethical dilemmas in channel management:
questions.explanation: The gray market. The gray market consists of businesses and individuals selling goods that have not been imported legally. While not technically illegal, these products are not officially licensed for distribution in the country they are being sold in. As a result, the products may not be up to standard and may lack important features such as a warranty. Exploitation and coercion are unethical behaviors that use scare tactics or power to force a business or individual to do something. A slotting allowance is a fee charged to a vendor by a retail establishment to place the vendor's products on the shelves. Exploitation, slotting allowance, and coercion are all ethical dilemmas in channel management; however, they are not demonstrated in this example.
questions.source: Northrup, L. (2017, May 10). What is the gray market, and why should I care? Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://consumerist.com/2013/05/09/what-is-the-gray-market-and-why-should-i-care/index.html

performanceIndicator.text: Describe ethical considerations in channel management

questions.question: Melissa's Pet Supplies has always ordered cat food from the same wholesaler. But when a shipment arrived a week late, the managers of the pet store decided to rethink the agreement with their supplier. This is an example of a __________ conflict.
questions.explanation: Vertical. A vertical conflict involves a disagreement between two channel members of different levels. A conflict between a supplier and a retailer, for example, constitutes a vertical conflict. A horizontal conflict is a disagreement between channel members at the same level within the channel. A multichannel conflict is a disagreement among members of multiple channels. Producer conflict is not a term used to describe a channel conflict.
questions.source: Mack, S. (2018, June 26). Horizontal and vertical marketing conflicts. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://smallbusiness.chron.com/horizontal-vertical-marketing-conflicts-65325.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of channel-member relationships

questions.question: Chase Bank partnered with Amazon to offer an Amazon.com rewards Visa. Amazon benefits from the partnership through greater sales, and Chase benefits by achieving greater brand exposure and new customers. This is an example of
questions.explanation: An affinity partnership. An affinity partnership is a partnership between two companies that is beneficial for each. Amazon's partnership with Chase Bank is an example of an affinity partner relationship, not business-to-business marketing or effective channel management. Business-to-business marketing is marketing designed for business customers rather than final consumers. Channel management refers to the processes by which marketers ensure that products are distributed to customers efficiently and effectively. Allocation partnership is not generally a term used to describe business relationships.
questions.source: Marketing-Schools.org. (2012). Affinity marketing. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.marketing-schools.org/types-of-marketing/affinity-marketing.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of affinity partner relationships

questions.question: Which of the following behaviors is an effective way to encourage and support a speaker:
questions.explanation: Maintaining eye contact. Maintaining eye contact is a good way to encourage a speaker and show your support for him/her. Speakers generally appreciate audience members that practice active listening because it shows respect and support. Using your phone, avoiding eye contact, and interrupting the speaker are all examples of poor listening skills and demonstrate a lack of support and respect for the speaker.
questions.source: Seeds for Change. (n.d.). Active listening. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.seedsforchange.org.uk/activelistening

performanceIndicator.text: Explain communication techniques that support and encourage a speaker

questions.question: When Chris facilitates group discussions, he tries to avoid influencing the conversation with his own personal biases and judgments. Chris is demonstrating which characteristic of an effective discussion leader:
questions.explanation: Objectivity. Objectivity is essential for group discussion leaders, because it allows for each person's opinion to be heard and evaluated without the bias of the facilitator. By trying to avoid influencing the conversation, Chris is demonstrating objectivity—not necessarily passiveness, subjectivity, or passive-aggression. Subjectivity means relying on personal bias and judgment. Passive-aggression is a tendency to display indirect hostility toward others. Passiveness means allowing things to happen without doing anything.
questions.source: Dlugan, A. (2015, August 16). How to lead a discussion group. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://sixminutes.dlugan.com/group-discussion-lead/

performanceIndicator.text: Facilitate (lead) group discussions

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding employees' use of social media is true:

options.A: When employees make negative comments about their company, it generates positive publicity.
options.B: An employee's personal social media pages have no impact on the company.
options.C: An employee's social media “brand” can impact the company's overall image.
options.D: Employees of large companies should never be allowed to have personal social media pages.

questions.explanation: An employee's social media “brand” can impact the company's overall image. Employees are often the “face” of a company. As a result, anything that an employee posts on social media—positive or negative—can impact his/her company's overall brand. Employees that make negative comments about their company do not generate positive publicity; rather, negative comments usually generate negative publicity for the company. Employees of any size company should not be banned from having personal social media pages. However, they should be trained in proper social media etiquette so that they don't risk harming the company's reputation.
questions.source: Lewis, J. (2012, March 23). Workplace challenges associated with employees' social media use. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.acc.com/legalresources/quickcounsel/wcawesmu.cfm

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the impact of a person's social media brand on the achievement of organizational objectives

questions.question: Which of the following conversations among employees would be considered lateral communication:

options.A: Rob is meeting with his boss to discuss his performance at work this quarter.
options.B: Jenny is discussing the upcoming company sales meeting with fellow salespeople.
options.C: Martin, a mid-level manager, is on a conference call with his company's board of directors.
options.D: Eli is holding a training session for his company's newly-hired employees.

questions.explanation: Jenny is discussing the upcoming company sales meeting with fellow salespeople. Lateral communication is communication exchanged among employees on the same hierarchical level. For example, a salesperson having a conversation with other salespeople is an example of lateral communication. Having a conversation with a boss or a company leader would be considered upward communication, not lateral communication. Holding a training session for new employees is an example of downward communication, not lateral communication.
questions.source: Rawes, E.M. (2017, September 26). Types of communication in the workplace. Retrieved January 10, 2018, from https://bizfluent.com/info-7742528-types-communication-workplace.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of staff communication

questions.question: Sportswear brand Nike strives to provide innovation and inspiration for all athletes. This is Nike's brand
questions.explanation: Promise. A brand promise is the specific benefit that customers can expect from using the good/service and interacting with the company. Nike's brand promise is to provide innovation and inspiration for all athletes. Nike's slogan is the well-known phrase "Just do it." A company's brand experience is just that—the experience that its customers have with the brand. Brand awareness is the level of knowledge that customers have of a brand.
questions.source: LAP-CR-006—Share the Promise (Identifying Brand Promise)

performanceIndicator.text: Identify company's brand promise

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding customer experience management (CEM) and customer relationship management (CRM) is true:

options.A: CRM is more customer-centric than CEM because it strives to create the best possible experience for customers.
options.B: CEM tends to focus on customers' needs, whereas CRM tends to focus on the business's needs.
options.C: One of the main goals of CRM is creating customer advocacy—word-of-mouth promotion and referrals to other potential customers.
options.D: CEM uses touchpoints to learn something valuable about the customer—something that the company can benefit from.

questions.explanation: CEM tends to focus on customers' needs, whereas CRM tends to focus on the business's needs. Customer experience management includes the strategies, processes, and policies a business uses to meet or exceed customer expectations and to provide customers with outstanding experiences at every touchpoint. Another main goal of CEM is creating customer advocacy—word-of-mouth promotion and referrals to other potential customers. CRM, on the other hand, is defined as the strategies, processes, technology, and people a business uses to build, maintain, and maximize the long-term value of customer relationships. CRM is more business-centric than CEM, and uses touchpoints to learn something valuable about the customer that the company can benefit from.
questions.source: LAP-CR-016—Know When To Hold 'Em (Nature of Customer Relationship Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of customer relationship management

questions.question: Which of the following business activities includes planning, maintaining, monitoring, controlling, and reporting the use of financial resources:
questions.explanation: Financial analysis. Financial analysis is the process of planning, maintaining, monitoring, controlling, and reporting the use of financial resources. Information management is the process of accessing, processing, maintaining, evaluating, and disseminating business knowledge, facts, or data. Human resources management is the process of planning, staffing, leading, and organizing employees. Operations are the day-to-day activities required for continued business functioning.
questions.source: LAP-EC-071—Strictly Business (Business Activities)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of business activities

questions.question: Allocating the right people and resources to a specific job results in more efficient and successful processes. This is the basic principle of
questions.explanation: Specialization. Specialization is the process of making the best use of resources in the production of goods and services. Specialization results in more efficient and successful processes. This is not the basic principle of employee training, concentration of skills, or labor unions.
questions.source: LAP-EC-007—Divide and Conquer (Specialization and Division of Labor)

performanceIndicator.text: Analyze impact of specialization/division of labor on productivity

questions.question: In 2016, a pair of running shoes cost $45. In 2017, that same pair of running shoes cost $55. Assuming that nothing else changed except the price of the shoes, this example most likely demonstrates
questions.explanation: Inflation. The main effect of inflation is reducing the purchasing power of the dollar. In other words, your money won't buy as much tomorrow as it will today. A pair of shoes rising in price over one year is an example of inflation—not shifting trends, deflation, or advertising power. If deflation was the case, the price of the shoes would have dropped. Shifting trends and advertising power may be factors in rising prices in certain cases, but this example clearly states that nothing changed except the price of the shoes.
questions.source: LAP-EC-028—Up, Up, and Away (Inflation)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the economic impact of inflation on business

questions.question: Cultures that readily show emotion are __________, whereas __________ cultures keep emotions controlled and subdued.
questions.explanation: Affective; neutral. One difference in nonverbal communication among cultures is the degree of emotion that is shown during a conversation. Affective cultures are those that readily show emotions, whereas neutral cultures keep emotions controlled and subdued. High-context cultures are those that rely heavily on nonverbal communication to get messages across. Low-context cultures are those that rely more on verbal communication.
questions.source: LAP-EC-045—On Top of the World (Impact of Culture on Global Trade)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the impact of cultural and social environments on global trade

questions.question: After an up-and-coming small business relocated to Springfield, the city enjoyed an economic boom and an increase in job openings for its citizens. This is an example of

options.A: the disadvantage for companies that move into struggling towns.
options.B: how corporations harm the growth of small businesses.
options.C: the positive impact of entrepreneurship on local economies.
options.D: small businesses driving out a town's larger corporations.

questions.explanation: The positive impact of entrepreneurship on local economies. Small businesses often have a positive impact on the communities they operate in by ushering in growth and innovation. Small businesses also help local economies by providing employment to people who may have otherwise been jobless. This example does not demonstrate how corporations harm the growth of small businesses, the disadvantage for companies that move into struggling towns, or how small businesses drive out a town's larger corporations.
questions.source: Brown, J. (2018, October 15). How important are small businesses to local economies? Retrieved January 10, 2018, from http://smallbusiness.chron.com/important-small-businesses-local-economies-5251.html

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the impact of small business/entrepreneurship on market economies

questions.question: Kalea is searching for a post-graduation job. She is looking for a position where she can utilize her writing and interpersonal communication skills. She is avoiding jobs that require math, since math is a subject she struggles with in school. Kalea has most likely

options.B: sold herself short in her job search.
options.C: made set-in-stone plans for her career.

questions.explanation: Assessed her strengths and weaknesses. It's important to assess your strengths and weaknesses when applying for a job. By applying to jobs where she can utilize her unique skills, it's clear that Kalea has assessed her strengths and weaknesses. Being realistic about her strengths and weaknesses does not mean that Kalea is selling herself short in her job search, underestimated her own skills, or that she has made set-in-stone plans for her career. Rather, it suggests that Kalea is taking the right steps toward a fulfilling career that maximizes her unique talents.
questions.source: LAP-EI-017—Assess for Success (Assessing Personal Strengths and Weaknesses)

performanceIndicator.text: Assess personal strengths and weaknesses

questions.question: Tanya's coworkers describe her as adaptable, cooperative, enthusiastic, and optimistic. When she comes across a problem at work, Tanya figures out how to solve it without being asked. In other words, Tanya shows
questions.explanation: Initiative. Initiative is the willingness to act without having to be told to do so. People who demonstrate initiative are willing to accept and seek out additional or even unpleasant duties. By figuring out how to solve a problem at work without being asked, Tanya is demonstrating initiative, not necessarily aggressiveness, empathy, or respect.
questions.source: LAP-EI-240—Hustle! (Taking Initiative at Work)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the importance of demonstrating initiative

questions.question: Selena really wants to play soccer with her friends, but she knows she needs to finish her chemistry project first. She works until the project is finished. In this situation, Selena is demonstrating
questions.explanation: Self-discipline. In this situation, Selena is demonstrating self-discipline, or an ability to stay committed to an important task even when it's difficult. Self-discipline is a helpful character trait to possess when learning to take responsibility for decisions and actions. Self-control is the ability to appropriately restrain your emotions and actions. Honesty is truthfulness. Attention to detail refers to being careful with tasks instead of producing sloppy work.
questions.source: LAP-EI-075—It's Up to You (Taking Responsibility for Decisions and Actions)

performanceIndicator.text: Take responsibility for decisions and actions

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of constructive criticism:

options.A: "Why didn't you pass the ball to Mike? He was wide open—we could have won the game!"
options.B: “You're obviously not very good at public speaking. You shouldn't even bother trying out for the debate team.”
options.C: “Your report is excellent, but it would be even better if you incorporated more primary resources to support your argument.”
options.D: “I thought your presentation was boring—that topic was so bland!”

questions.explanation: “Your report is excellent, but it would be even better if you incorporated more primary resources to support your argument.” Constructive criticism is feedback that points out mistakes or weaknesses for the purpose of helping a person improve a specific behavior. Constructive criticism is private, thoughtful, nonjudgmental, nonthreatening, immediate, specific, and factual. The other options provided are judgmental, threatening, and unhelpful for the recipient.
questions.source: LAP-EI-015—Grin and Bear It (Using Feedback for Personal Growth)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of feedback for personal growth

questions.question: In the communication process, one of the most important responsibilities of a receiver is to

options.A: practice active listening at all times.
options.B: be as quiet as possible and avoid speaking.
options.D: take meticulous notes during the conversation.

questions.explanation: Practice active listening at all times. By practicing active listening, receivers can ensure that they fully understand the sender's message. While being quiet and paying attention is important during active listening, it is not necessary for the receiver to completely avoid speaking. Receivers should not interrupt the speaker at any time—doing so is rude and can cause the sender to lose his/her train of thought. It is usually not necessary for receivers to take notes during a conversation.
questions.source: LAP-EI-140—More Than Just Talk (Effective Communication)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of effective communications

questions.question: Which of the following is a requirement for an effective negotiation:
questions.explanation: Mutual respect. It's important for all parties in a negotiation to show respect. Negotiators may not agree with what the other party says, but being rude, dismissive, or pushy won't help the negotiation. Instead, negotiators should be informed, objective, and thoughtful. It's also important for negotiators to be patient, flexible, and aware of their strategy and goals. Impatience, inflexibility, and a lack of awareness of one's goals are likely to harm the outcome of a negotiation.
questions.source: LAP-EI-062—Make It a Win-Win (Negotiation in Business)

questions.question: What happens during the emergence stage of a conflict?
questions.explanation: The conflict is realized. During the emergence stage of conflict, the participants become aware of the conflict and experience mental and physical reactions. Complaints are aired during the escalation stage of conflict. Options are discussed during the de-escalation stage. Resolution is the last stage of conflict.
questions.source: LAP-EI-007—Stop the Madness (Conflict Resolution in Business)

performanceIndicator.text: Use conflict-resolution skills

questions.question: Which of the following is the most positive way to deal with changes in a work environment:

options.A: View them as an opportunity to learn something new.
options.B: Realize that they will happen whether you like it or not.
options.C: Reduce stress by doing things the same way you always have.
options.D: Convince others that the changes are not necessary.

questions.explanation: View them as an opportunity to learn something new. Viewing changes as opportunities to grow and learn new skills demonstrates a positive, adaptable mindset. Realizing changes will happen helps a person accept changes but is not as positive as seeing them as a way to grow. Doing things the same way or convincing others that changes aren't necessary are not positive or productive ways to deal with change.
questions.source: LAP-EI-023—Go With the Flow (Demonstrating Adaptability)

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate adaptability

questions.question: One way to protect yourself against identity theft is to

options.A: open every email you have been sent.
options.B: give out your bank account number by phone.
options.C: limit the number of credit cards you have.
options.D: carry your passport and birth certificate with you.

questions.explanation: Limit the number of credit cards you have. One step you can take to avoid identity theft is to limit the number of credit cards you have. The fewer credit accounts you have in your name, the easier it will be for you to keep track of your activity—and to identify any suspicious purchases. It is unwise to give out your bank account number by phone unless you can absolutely verify that the call is legitimate. Similarly, you should not open emails unless you can verify who the sender is. Carrying personal documents around with you is not a good idea, since someone could easily steal them.
questions.source: Fight Identity Theft. (1999-2018). Other prevention tips. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.fightidentitytheft.com/ssn.html

performanceIndicator.text: Protect against identity theft

questions.question: Every month, Jonathon pays a premium to a company in exchange for the company's promise to provide the funds needed for potential future losses. In other words, Jonathon is paying for
questions.explanation: Insurance. Insurance is a contractual agreement in which one company (the insurer) will pay for specified losses incurred by the other individual or company (the insured) in return for installment payments (premium). In this example, Jonathon is paying for some type of insurance—not tax deductions, government assistance, or retirement.
questions.source: Money Instructor. (2002-2019). Insurance basics: What can be covered? Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.moneyinstructor.com/doc/insurancecoverage.asp

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the concept of insurance

questions.question: Which of the following examples demonstrates the need for accountants to pay attention to the public interest:

options.A: An accountant provides information about economic growth.
options.B: A company makes its financial statements as complex as possible.
options.C: Accountants focus on only what is best for their clients.
options.D: Accountants keep their clients' information private.

questions.explanation: An accountant provides information about economic growth. Many people can be affected by the information provided by an accountant. Therefore, accountants have a responsibility to look out for the greater good of the public as a whole, not just themselves or their clients. Providing information about economic growth can have an impact on society. Making financial statements as complex as possible goes against the principle of transparency/full disclosure. Focusing on only what is best for clients goes against the principle of the public interest. Finally, keeping clients' information private is confidentiality.
questions.source: LAP-FI-351—With Due Care (The Role of Ethics in Accounting)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in accounting

questions.question: Marjorie is an intern in the finance department of a local business. Her boss asks her to write a report on the company's financial status at the end of the accounting period. Which of the following financial statements would provide Marjorie with the most information for her report:
questions.explanation: Balance sheet. The balance sheet is one of a business's key financial statements. It shows how much money a company has, how much money it owes, and how much belongs to its owners or stockholders. Sometimes called a statement of financial position, the balance sheet is usually described as a "snapshot" of the company's finances at a certain point in time. A cash flow statement is a financial summary with estimates as to when, where, and how much money will flow into and out of a business. An income statement describes the company's revenues, expenses, and profits/losses generated during the reporting period. Finally, a statement of retained earnings presents changes in equity during the reporting period. Marjorie's company's balance sheet would probably be the most helpful for her as she writes her report, since her boss is interested in obtaining a snapshot of the company's financial health at a specific point in time.
questions.source: LAP-FI-010—The Right Balance (The Nature of Balance Sheets)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of balance sheets

questions.question: Which of the following descriptions accurately represents the difference between finance and accounting:

options.A: The purpose of accounting is to boost the company's growth and reduce its overall risks.
options.B: The purpose of finance is to provide accurate and timely information about the company's finances at any point in time.
options.C: Finance focuses primarily on money management decisions, while accounting focuses on recordkeeping activities.
options.D: Accounting focuses primarily on money management decisions, while finance focuses on recordkeeping activities.

questions.explanation: Finance focuses primarily on money management decisions, while accounting focuses on recordkeeping activities. It can be difficult to tell the difference between finance and accounting—the two are closely interrelated and even overlap in some areas. However, there are several key differences between the finance and accounting functions. First, they are distinct in focus. The finance function primarily focuses on money management decisions, while accounting focuses on recordkeeping activities. The two functions are also different in their ultimate purposes. The purpose of the finance function is to boost the company's growth and to reduce its risks. The purpose of the accounting function is to provide accurate and timely information about the company's finances at any point in time.
questions.source: LAP-FI-007—Money Matters (Role of Finance)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of finance in business

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about marketing-information systems:

options.A: They may be slow to update during major business changes.
options.B: They are often not worth the money it costs to install them.
options.C: They are easy for employees, customers, and vendors to use.
options.D: They eliminate the need for marketing managers and staff.

questions.explanation: They may be slow to update during major business changes. Marketing-information systems are not without their limitations. They can be slow to update with new information during major business changes. They may be expensive to install, but that doesn't mean it isn't worth the cost and effort. Marketing-information systems aren't always easy to use, but training employees properly should help them become proficient. They do not eliminate the need for skilled marketing managers and staff.
questions.source: LAP-IM-002—Get the Facts Straight (Marketing-Information Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of the marketing-information management function

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a leading question that might make marketing research unethical:

options.A: What is your opinion of this advertisement?
options.B: Why is our product superior to that of the competition?
options.C: How many sales did you make this quarter?
options.D: Where did you buy our product?

questions.explanation: Why is our product superior to that of the competition? This is a leading question because it steers the respondent to answer in a particular way. It could reduce the objectivity and integrity of the marketing information. The other three questions are more open-ended and do not attempt to guide the participant to answering the question in a particular way.
questions.source: LAP-IM-025—Info With Integrity (Ethics in Marketing-Information Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in marketing-information management

questions.question: What is a common reason for a company to hire an outside research firm to conduct research on its behalf?

options.A: The company doesn't have sufficient funds for the research.
options.B: The company wants the research to remain biased.
options.C: The company does not have time to conduct the research.
options.D: The company has access to abundant external data.

questions.explanation: The company does not have time to conduct the research. The most common reason a company hires an outside research firm is because it does not have the time required to conduct the research. Since research needs to be unbiased to be valid, it's not likely a company would desire biased results. Research costs time and money to conduct regardless of who conducts it. If the company has access to abundant internal and external data, it's less likely to require an outside research firm.
questions.source: LAP-IM-010—Seek and Find (Marketing Research)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of marketing research

questions.question: Joanna is doing research on social media trends. To help her get started, she reads whitepapers and reports by respected media scholars. Joanna is engaging in __________ research.
questions.explanation: Secondary. Secondary research is research using data that have already been collected for some reason other than the research project on hand. In other words, the data already exist in some form. Reading whitepapers and reports is an example of secondary research. Primary research is original research done specifically for the project at hand. Primary research collects original data that have not been collected before. Quantitative and qualitative research are types of primary research.
questions.source: LAP-IM-281—What's the Source? (Obtaining Marketing-Research Data)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe options businesses use to obtain marketing research data (i.e., primary and secondary research)

questions.question: Jen's Ice Cream Shop has been facing declining sales ever since a new grocery store opened up next door. Jen thinks that the grocery store's cheap ice cream prices have driven people away from her shop. As a result, Jen decides to put up advertisements for her weekly specials on the grocery store's community board. She even lowers prices on some of her ice creams to be more competitive. However, after she does some research, Jen realizes that the cause of her declining sales isn't the grocery store, after all. It's the poor weather! This example best demonstrates the importance of

options.A: leveraging the business's strengths to help it succeed.
options.B: choosing a location away from other businesses.
options.C: opening a business in the appropriate climate.
options.D: addressing the root of a marketing problem.

questions.explanation: Addressing the root of a marketing problem. If a business tries to address the symptoms of a problem without actually discovering the real problem, the business risks wasting valuable time and resources. Jen's decision to jump into a plan of action without doing sufficient research demonstrates the importance of addressing the root of a marketing problem. If Jen had known that the weather was the reason for declining sales, she could come up with a more effective strategy to combat the issue. This example does not necessarily demonstrate the importance of choosing a location away from other businesses, opening a business in the appropriate climate, or leveraging the business's strengths to help it succeed.
questions.source: LAP-IM-282—What's the Problem? (Marketing Research Problems)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of marketing research problems/issues

questions.question: The Seven Hills Cola company believes that men will buy diet soda if masculine packaging is used. What type of marketing research would help the company collect the data it needs?
questions.explanation: Causal. To determine if a certain type of packaging will have an effect on men's purchasing behavior, the company should use causal research, which focuses on cause and effect and tests “what if?” theories. Exploratory research involves collecting information to help the business define its issue, situation, or concern. Descriptive research gathers specific information related to the identified issue, but it isn't typically used to test the effect of an independent variable on a dependent variable. Although every type of research should yield informative data, informative is not a type of research.
questions.source: LAP-IM-284—Better by Design (Marketing Research Design)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe methods used to design marketing research studies (i.e., descriptive, exploratory, and causal)

questions.question: Large corporations such as Walmart and Coca-Cola have too many people in their target markets to contact each individual for marketing research purposes. To make it easier to gather data about their customers, these companies usually

options.A: ignore parts of a target market.

questions.explanation: Use sampling methods. Why do marketers use samples for research purposes? The main reason for sampling is that contacting every single member of a target population (a process called a census) is often unrealistic or impossible. If a company has millions of potential customers, marketers cannot reasonably be expected to get in touch with every single one of them. Using a representative sample is a much quicker and much less expensive method of gathering data. Gathering data about employees does not necessarily help a company gain insight into customer preferences. Companies do not purposely ignore parts of a target market.
questions.source: LAP-IM-285—Take Your Pick (Nature of Sampling Plans)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of sampling plans (i.e., who, how many, how chosen)

questions.question: How can a business gain external information about the environment in which it operates?

options.A: Research industry trends through trade publications.
options.B: Examine service call records and product returns.
options.C: Track digital marketing analytics to determine the number of site visits.
options.D: Use sales volume analysis to assess the effectiveness of sales in a specific region.

questions.explanation: Research industry trends through trade publications. Trade publications provide information on the state of the industry, trends, and news in the field. Being informed about the industry in which a business operates is important when making marketing decisions. The number of site visits is data from digital marketing analytics that provides information about customers and the effectiveness of marketing campaigns, rather than about the external environment. Sales volume analysis is an internal analysis of sales performance and does not provide information about the outside environment. Service call records and product returns are internal sources of data.
questions.source: LAP-IM-184—Data Diving (Identifying Marketing Data)

performanceIndicator.text: Identify data monitored for marketing decision making

questions.question: Natasha is a marketing consultant. She recently conducted a focus group for a company that was interested in learning more about its middle-aged customers. The type of data she will collect from the focus group will likely be
questions.explanation: Qualitative. Qualitative data are descriptive and nonstatistical in nature. Common methods for gathering qualitative data are personal interviews, focus groups, and observation. Quantitative data are numbers and statistics—hard facts. Quantitative data can be classified as discrete or continuous. Discrete data can take on only integer values whereas continuous data can take on any value.
questions.source: LAP-IM-017—Hunting and Gathering (Data-Collection Methods)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe data-collection methods (e.g., observations, mail, diaries, phone, internet, discussion groups, interviews, scanners, tracking tools)

questions.question: Which of the following is a quality of a good survey:

options.A: A single focus for each question

questions.explanation: A single focus for each question. Survey questions should have a single focus so that respondents know exactly what they are being asked. Questions with multiple focuses are confusing and often result in skewed results. Instructions on surveys should be clear and concise, not vague. Questions should be objective and unbiased and should not “lead” respondents to a certain response.
questions.source: StatPac Inc. (2017). Qualities of a good question. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.statpac.com/surveys/question-qualities.htm

performanceIndicator.text: Explain characteristics of effective data-collection instruments

questions.question: Jake is a data analyst. Before analyzing large surveys, he prepares the results using a numerical sorting system. For example, if a question asks for an individual's gender, he records the responses “male” and “female” as “1” or “2,” respectively. What technique is Jake using to process the marketing data?
questions.explanation: Coding. Data analysis is made easier by coding, a process that transforms data into a form that is suitable for (oftentimes computer-facilitated) analysis. Coding involves assigning a code or number to a specific data point so that the data can be easily categorized and analyzed. Descriptive analysis and inferential analysis are both forms of data analysis that take place after coding has occurred. Decoding is not a term used to describe data analysis processes.
questions.source: California State University, Long Beach. (n.d.). Data entry issues. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://web.csulb.edu/~msaintg/ppa696/696codes.htm

performanceIndicator.text: Explain techniques for processing marketing data

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the types of statistics in marketing research is true:

options.A: Inferential statistics simply describe or show what the data are.
options.B: Researchers use descriptive statistics to make conclusions beyond the data alone.
options.C: Descriptive statistics simply describe or show what the data are.
options.D: Researchers use inferential statistics to provide a concise summary of the data.

questions.explanation: Descriptive statistics simply describe or show what the data are. Descriptive statistics are used to summarize and describe data. Researchers use descriptive statistics to provide a concise summary of the data they are studying, not to make conclusions beyond the data. Inferential statistics are used to make conclusions or inferences based on the data and about the broader population.
questions.source: Kenton, W. (2018, May 25). Descriptive statistics. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/d/descriptive_statistics.asp

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of descriptive statistics in marketing decision making

questions.question: Omar is conducting research for a school project. After carefully selecting a 50-person sample, he calls each person to ask for his/her participation in his study. Unfortunately, Omar is unable to reach 22 people in his sample. What type of research error has occurred?
questions.explanation: Non-response error. A non-response error occurs when the sample that is actually obtained is different from the sample that was originally selected. Non-response errors occur because either: a) the respondent could not be contacted or b) the respondent refused to participate. This situation does not describe a sampling error, an interviewer error, or a response error. A sampling error occurs when the sample is not representative of the population in question. An interviewer error occurs when the personality or mannerisms of the interviewer impacts the responses of the participants. A response error is any error that results from a respondent providing untrue or incorrect information.
questions.source: Kumar, R.V. (n.d.). Errors in research design. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.angelfire.com/falcon/neeraja-rohit/3y_mr/type_error.pdf

performanceIndicator.text: Identify sources of error in a research project (e.g., response errors, interviewer errors, non-response errors, sample design)

questions.question: Identify the problem in the following survey question: “What is your opinion on the upcoming school board election and the proposal to build a new elementary school?”

options.A: The question is asking two different things.
options.D: The question is misleading and confusing.

questions.explanation: The question is asking two different things. Effective survey questions should have a single focus so that respondents know how to answer. This question should be separated into two questions. The question in this example is not ambiguous or misleading, nor does it use unfamiliar terminology.
questions.source: Survey Monkey. (1999-2019). 5 common survey question mistakes that'll ruin your data. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.surveymonkey.com/mp/5-common-survey-mistakes-ruin-your-data/

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate questionnaire design (e.g., types of questions, question wording, routing, sequencing, length, layout)

questions.question: A(n) __________ is something you hold to be true or real, while a(n) __________ is a good or bad feeling about something.
questions.explanation: Belief; attitude. A belief is something that you hold to be true or real. An attitude, on the other hand, is a good or bad feeling about something that forms over time and is unlikely to change. An expectation is something you anticipate to happen based on familiarity or past experience.
questions.source: LAP-MK-014—Cause and Effect (Buying Behavior)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain factors that influence customer/client/business buying behavior

questions.question: Which of the following best describes tactics:

options.A: They are a plan of action for achieving goals.
options.B: They are specific actions used to carry out strategies.
options.C: They are not essential for making a plan work.
options.D: They are objectives a company plans to fulfill.

questions.explanation: They are specific actions used to carry out strategies. Tactics are short-term actions that are used to carry out strategies. Strategies are plans of action for achieving goals. Goals are objectives a company plans to fulfill. Tactics are essential for making a plan work.
questions.source: LAP-MP-002—Pick the Mix (Nature of Marketing Strategies)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of marketing strategies

questions.question: Stef and Amy are studying the athletic shoe market. They have discovered that fashion-focused buyers as well as high-performing athletes prefer athletic shoes with a well-known brand name and identity. Stef and Amy have identified a __________ market.
questions.explanation: Target. A target market typically consists of different groups that share the same wants, needs, or other characteristics. Mass marketing refers to marketing the same item to every potential customer, not to specific groups. Fashion-focused buyers and high-performing athletes are not examples of demographics (e.g., gender, religion, social status) or life stage (e.g., child, teen, parent).
questions.source: LAP-MP-003—Have We Met? (Market Identification)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of market and market identification

questions.question: The marketing department of a clothing company decides to focus on obtaining a bigger market share. Under which section of the marketing plan would they include this goal?
questions.explanation: Marketing strategies and programs. The goal of obtaining a bigger market share is known as growth strategy and is a general marketing strategy that should be detailed in the marketing strategies and programs section. The performance and implementation section explains expected results and how progress will be measured. The desired target market section includes demographic information on the target market that the company desires to reach. The situation analysis provides a “snapshot” of the current marketing situation.
questions.source: LAP-MP-007—A Winning Plan (Nature of Marketing Plans)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of marketing plans

questions.question: Megan is using past sales records, accounting records, market research, and customer surveys to make predictions about future sales for her company. Megan is conducting
questions.explanation: Quantitative forecasting. Quantitative sales forecasting is based on the analysis of hard facts or numerical data. For a weather forecast, these data would come from sources such as weather balloons, radar, etc. For a business, the information comes from both internal and external sources. Internal information may come in forms such as past sales records, accounting records, financial statements, market research, customer surveys, and product research. Qualitative sales forecasting is based on expert opinion and personal experience. When using this approach, businesses talk to knowledgeable people who have a strong understanding of the marketplace. These sources may include experienced managers, suppliers, and other industry experts. In this example, Megan is conducting quantitative analysis, not qualitative analysis, statistical analysis, or inventory analysis.
questions.source: LAP-MP-005—Futurecast (The Nature of Sales Forecasts)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of sales forecasts

questions.question: When searching for reliable, relevant information on the Internet, it's best to

options.A: find one source you like and trust that it is reliable.
options.B: search for older rather than newer content.
options.C: visit websites run by students and nonprofessionals.
options.D: stick to unbiased sources that present two sides of every story.

questions.explanation: Stick to unbiased sources that present two sides of every story. When searching for reliable, relevant information online, it's important to locate objective, unbiased sources. News organizations and encyclopedias are generally good options for unbiased information, but it's still wise to visit multiple sources to confirm that the information you are reading is unbiased. For the most relevant information possible, you should search for newer—not older—content. Visiting websites run by students and nonprofessionals may be helpful as supplements to your research, but you should generally use professional websites (run by news organizations, encyclopedias, governments, etc.) as your main sources of information.
questions.source: Goodwill Community Foundation, Inc. (2012). How to judge online information. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.gcflearnfree.org/searchbetter/judging-online-information/1/

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: Jeff is a data analyst at a consumer research company. When he needs to access a certain document, he knows exactly where and how to find it. This is an example of how information management helps businesses
questions.explanation: Save time and money. For a business to run efficiently, information must be managed and organized so it can be found quickly whenever it is needed. And in business, where time is money, this is cost-effective as well. Information management saves businesses time and money by controlling information overload, cutting down on enormous paper trails, and maintaining a higher level of productivity. Information management also helps businesses serve customers more effectively, maintain credibility, and comply with laws—but these benefits are not demonstrated in this example.
questions.source: LAP-NF-110—In the Know (Nature of Information Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of information management

questions.question: The first step in creating a basic web page is

options.D: designing the content pages of the website.

questions.explanation: Registering your website's domain name. The first thing you should do when creating a basic website is choosing and registering a domain name (www.WebsiteABC.com, for example). Once you have chosen and registered a domain name, you can move on to designing and writing the content for your website, as well as creating a home page.
questions.source: Marsan, J. (2017, November 17). How to make a small business website in 5 simple steps. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://fitsmallbusiness.com/small-business-website/#Design

performanceIndicator.text: Create and post basic web page

questions.question: Megan's boss asked her to conduct a study on her company's customers. Based on her findings, Megan concludes that the median age of the people in the sample is 43. This means that

options.A: 43 is the age that occurred the most in Megan's population sample.
options.B: 43 is the arithmetic average of all of the ages in Megan's population sample.
options.C: Megan's boss should assume that most of the company's customers are elderly.
options.D: if all the ages were listed from youngest to oldest, 43 would be the number in the middle.

questions.explanation: If all the ages were listed from youngest to oldest, 43 would be the number in the middle. The median is the middle number in a set of numbers. This means that if all the ages in Megan's sample were listed from youngest to oldest, 43 would be the number in the middle. The arithmetic average of a set of numbers is called the mean, and the number that occurs the most in a sample is called the mode. There is not enough information given in this example to determine whether Megan's boss should assume that most of the customers are elderly.
questions.source: Cherry, K. (2018, March 9). How to identify and calculate the mean, median, and mode. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.verywellmind.com/how-to-identify-and-calculate-the-mean-median-or-mode-2795785

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret statistical findings

questions.question: An example of a project is __________, whereas __________ is an example of business operations.

options.A: creating a business plan; organizing a conference
options.B: manufacturing a car; designing a car
options.C: designing a new product; selling the product
options.D: building relationships with customers; communicating with suppliers

questions.explanation: Designing a new product; selling the product. A project is a short-term undertaking that creates a unique good or service. Projects are short-term, have a distinct beginning and end, and occur outside the scope of a business's operations. Business operations are permanent, ongoing, and keep the business going on a day-to-day basis. Designing a new product is short-term, has a beginning and end, and occurs outside the scope of regular business operations, so it is a project. Selling products is an example of business operations because is a permanent, ongoing activity that keeps the business going. Manufacturing a car is also an example of business operations, while designing a car is a project. Creating a business plan and organizing a conference could both be considered projects. Finally, building relationships with customers and communicating with suppliers are both examples of business operations rather than projects.
questions.source: LAP-OP-158—Projected To Win (Nature of Project Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of project management

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding a quality culture is true:

options.A: Peer involvement is generally ineffective when it comes to encouraging a culture of quality.
options.B: Employees will generally maintain quality even if company leaders don't emphasize it.
options.C: Company leaders have the largest impact on a business's culture of quality.
options.D: The more empowered employees feel, the less likely they are to maintain a culture of quality.

questions.explanation: Company leaders have the largest impact on a business's culture of quality. Quality flows from the top down. When company leaders care about quality, so will the rest of the company's employees. Employees generally will not maintain a quality culture if company leaders don't emphasize it. Peer involvement is another good way to encourage a culture of quality. Employees are more likely to practice quality management if their coworkers are doing so. Finally, empowered employees are more likely to hold themselves and their work to higher quality standards than those that are not empowered.
questions.source: Leadership Review. (2014, December 12). How to build a culture of quality for your organization. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.leadershipreview.net/building-a-culture-of-quality

questions.question: Simon, an employee at a movie theater, never takes popcorn or snacks from behind the counter unless he pays for them. He knows that the theater would run into trouble if the employees routinely took food without paying for it. Simon's behavior is an example of how employees can

options.A: be punished for breaking the rules.
options.B: act as salespeople for the company.

questions.explanation: Contribute to expense control. Employees can help keep expenses down by respecting company property and paying for whatever they use or take. Simon's behavior is an example of how employees can contribute to expense control—not act as salespeople, be punished for breaking the rules, or increase expenses for the company.
questions.source: LAP-OP-025—Buck Busters (Employee Role in Expense Control)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain employee's role in expense control

questions.question: A soft-drink manufacturer needs to keep the right amount of sodas on hand to satisfy customer demand without producing excess product that will go unused. This is an example of which aspect of supply chain management?
questions.explanation: Inventory management. Inventory management is the process of supervising and controlling the number of finished products a company has in stock. Inventory is a balancing act—companies don't want to overproduce or underproduce products. Customer service, cost management, and logistics management are also important components of the supply chain, but they are not necessarily demonstrated in this example.
questions.source: Marion, G. (2018, April 23). Introduction to supply chain management. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.thebalancesmb.com/logistics-4161402

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of supply chain

questions.question: Owen and his lawyer have an agreement that protects the sensitive information that Owen shares. According to the agreement, Owen's attorney can't share his personal information with anyone else. This is an example of an agreement regarding
questions.explanation: Confidentiality. Confidentiality refers to the agreement of an individual or party not to share the sensitive information of another individual or party. Most lawyers have confidentiality agreements with their clients that protect the sensitive details of the clients' cases from being shared with others. While similar to confidentiality, privacy and security differ in important ways. Privacy is the right of an individual to keep his/her information to him/herself, while security is the protection of sensitive data or items that are housed in a database or other storage facility. Transparency refers to openness or honesty. This example best describes a confidentiality agreement.
questions.source: Ashe-Edmunds, S. (2018, June 29). What is the meaning of confidentiality in the workplace? Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://work.chron.com/meaning-confidentiality-workplace-21886.html

questions.question: Carly is inventive, imaginative, and innovative. In other words, she is able to develop something original, see something that's “not there,” and make changes or improvements to old ways of doing things. Carly could best be described as
questions.explanation: Creative. Creativity is the ability to generate unique ideas, possibilities, and solutions. People that are creative usually possess inventiveness, imagination, and innovation. Based on the information given, Carly can best be described as creative—not necessarily independent, a rule-follower, or a troublemaker.
questions.source: LAP-PD-012—Imagine That (Demonstrating Creativity)

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate appropriate creativity

questions.question: Which of the following sources would best help a high school student learn more about potential careers in his/her region or state:
questions.explanation: Employees in the desired field. Employees in the desired field are an excellent source of career information for students. Talking to people with firsthand knowledge of the position or occupation that you are interested in is a great way to learn more about daily life in the field. Tax preparation centers, town visitor information booths, and retired relatives would not necessarily provide relevant career information for students.
questions.source: Butler, J. (2017, July 6). The importance of job shadowing. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.educationquest.org/blog/importance-job-shadowing/

performanceIndicator.text: Identify sources of career information

questions.question: Maria is interested in completing an internship in her desired field. She knows that an internship can help her

options.A: obtain a position that requires prior experience.
options.B: skip an entry-level job and go straight to management.
options.C: guarantee her position at the company she wants to work at.
options.D: become qualified for jobs that require advanced degrees.

questions.explanation: Obtain a position that requires prior experience. Internships can help individuals with little or no background in a certain field become qualified for jobs that require more substantial experience. However, an internship cannot necessarily take the place of an entry-level job—and Maria will most likely not be able to go straight to management once she enters her desired field. An internship also does not guarantee her position at the company she would like to work for or qualify her for jobs that require advanced degrees.
questions.source: McKay, D. (2019, January 9). Why internships are an essential part of your education. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.thebalancecareers.com/should-you-do-an-internship-525756

performanceIndicator.text: Describe techniques for obtaining work experience (e.g., volunteer activities, internships)

questions.question: The staff at Money First Bank are organized hierarchically. The CEO of the bank is at the top, followed by the assistant managers, the department heads, and the general employees. This is the bank's
questions.explanation: Chain of command. Simply put, a chain of command is the flow of authority within an organization. Chains of command are often organized hierarchically, meaning that authority flows from top to bottom. This example demonstrates a chain of command, not an emergency plan, a public relations scheme, or a recruiting strategy.
questions.source: LAP-PD-252—Don't Cheat the Chain (Following Chain of Command)

performanceIndicator.text: Follow chain of command

questions.question: Orlando's main job duties include resolving complaints and returns, answering questions, and creating goodwill. What marketing career does Orlando have?
questions.explanation: Customer service. Customer service jobs usually involve dealing directly with customers and creating goodwill. Customer service professionals may answer customer questions, resolve complaints and returns, process orders, and many other duties that relate to customer satisfaction. Marketing management focuses on all marketing functions, including channel management, marketing-information management, pricing, product/service management, promotion, and selling. Service marketers must market services, which are intangible—they can't be touched, seen, smelled, heard, or tasted. Marketing research professionals are in charge of figuring out what customers need and want, and why they do what they do.
questions.source: LAP-PD-024—Career Opportunities in Marketing

performanceIndicator.text: Explain employment opportunities in marketing

questions.question: In 2011, a used book on the genetics of flies made waves on the Internet when its price rose into the millions on Amazon.com. The cause? A pricing algorithm gone wrong. The seller had an automated system set up to immediately raise the price of the book whenever a competitor increased its price for the same item. This is an example of the

options.A: benefits of setting up an automatic pricing system online.
options.B: risks of using technology for pricing items online.
options.C: advantages of selling items on Amazon and other online marketplaces.
options.D: inability of third-party sellers to make a profit through Amazon.

questions.explanation: Risks of using technology for pricing items online. Technology, such as automated pricing tools, can benefit a company by reducing the amount of time and manpower required to set prices. However, there are definite risks associated with pricing technology—such as the possibility for the technology to backfire and set astronomical prices for items such as the used book on flies. This example demonstrates the risks associated with using technology for pricing, not the benefits of setting up automated pricing systems, the advantages of selling items on Amazon, or the inability of third-party sellers to make a profit through Amazon.
questions.source: Sherman, E. (2013, January 16). How to use technology to win a price war. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.inc.com/erik-sherman/how-to-use-repricing-software-to-your-advantage.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of technology in the pricing function

questions.question: In an attempt to undercut the competition, a large technology store recently lowered its prices on a popular computer so that other stores selling the item would have to lower their prices as well. The store hopes that by lowering the price significantly, it can drive out competing stores in the area. The technology store is using
questions.explanation: Predatory pricing. Predatory pricing is a form of anticompetitive pricing used by a company that is dominant in its market to prevent new or existing competitors from gaining part of its market share. Predatory pricing involves temporarily lowering the price of a product in order to end a competitive threat. Bait-and-switch advertising involves promoting a low-priced item to attract customers and then trying to sell those customers a higher priced item. Deceptive pricing involves tricking customers into thinking that they will pay a lower price for a product than they are actually supposed to. Price fixing is an agreement among competing sellers to maintain the prices of certain items at a certain level. This example demonstrates predatory pricing, not bait-and-switch advertising, deceptive pricing, or price fixing.
questions.source: Maxi-Pedia.com. (2017). Predatory pricing. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.maxi-pedia.com/predatory+pricing

performanceIndicator.text: Explain legal considerations for pricing

questions.question: The Salty Pretzel Company, which has been doing very well in the market, shifts its pricing objectives to maximize profits. Most likely, The Salty Pretzel Company is
questions.explanation: Trying to improve cash flow. The Salty Pretzel Company is using a profit-oriented pricing objective of maximizing profits. Because there is no indication that the company is in financial trouble, it is most likely trying to improve cash flow for one reason or another. If the company was trying to create an exclusive image, it would use a sales-oriented pricing objective to do so. The company already has market share and would lower prices to capture more. The company is most like to be increasing prices, not stabilizing them.
questions.source: LAP-PI-003—Make Cents (Factors Affecting Selling Price)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain factors affecting pricing decisions

questions.question: During the introduction stage of the product life cycle, profits are usually
questions.explanation: Extremely low. A product enters the market during the introduction stage. During this time, profits are usually extremely low or even nonexistent. That's because sales are usually slow at first—after all, customers are just now finding out that the product even exists. In addition, the costs of introducing a new product are very high. Researching and developing the product, testing it, producing it, and marketing it are all expensive ventures. Profits are not generally skyrocketing, steadily growing, or even remaining stable during the introduction stage.
questions.source: LAP-PM-024—Get a Life (Cycle) (Product Life Cycles)

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the impact of product life cycles on marketing decisions

questions.question: Which of the following is a result of managing products and services ethically:
questions.explanation: Positive company reputation. When products and services are managed ethically, customers are generally free from harm and satisfied with their purchases—resulting in greater profits and a positive company reputation. Ethical management of products and services does not result in increased risk for customers, lower profits for the company, or customer dissatisfaction.
questions.source: LAP-PM-040—Safe and Sound (Ethics in Product/Service Management)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain business ethics in product/service management

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios demonstrates market gap identification:

options.A: An airline recognizes the need for affordable flights for families.
options.B: A luxury car manufacturer adds extra features to appeal to its buyers.
options.C: A grocery store starts stocking a popular brand of breakfast cereal.
options.D: An educational television network becomes aware of its declining viewership.

questions.explanation: An airline recognizes the need for affordable flights for families. A market gap exists when sizeable groups of people have needs that are not being met by current products or services. An airline recognizing that families need affordable flights is an example of a market gap identification. Adding features to a product to appeal to current buyers, stocking a popular brand of cereal, and becoming aware of declining viewership are not examples of identifying a market gap.
questions.source: Marketing Donut. (2019). Spotting gaps in your market. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.marketingdonut.co.uk/market-research/spotting-gaps-in-your-market

performanceIndicator.text: Identify product opportunities

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of improving an existing product:

options.A: Selling contact lenses instead of eyeglasses
options.B: Including a pair of headphones in the sale of a tablet
options.C: Adding an enhanced camera to a smartphone
options.D: Developing new TV ads for a successful video game

questions.explanation: Adding an enhanced camera to a smartphone. Existing products, even those that are successful, can be a source of new product ideas. For example, adding a high-quality camera to a smartphone improves its functionality and makes it into something new. Including a pair of headphones with a tablet is an example of a complementary good. Selling contact lenses instead of glasses is a substitute good. Finally, developing new TV ads for a successful video game is not an improvement to the product, but rather a change in promotional strategy.
questions.source: LAP-PM-127—Unleash Your Mind (Techniques for Generating Product Ideas)

performanceIndicator.text: Identify methods/techniques to generate a product idea

questions.question: An employee at a factory must assemble 15 units. This is an example of a __________ standard.
questions.explanation: Quantity. Quantity standards specify the amount of work to be done. Production managers determine the minimum number of units to be produced each hour, day, or month by individual workers or groups of workers. This is not an example of a quality, time, or cost standard.
questions.source: LAP-PM-008—Raise the Bar (Grades and Standards)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the uses of grades and standards in marketing

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an express warranty:

options.A: A salesperson states that if a power washer breaks within the first year of owning it, the company will repair or replace it.
options.B: Television commercials advertise a power washer as the best heavy-duty cleaning device on the market.
options.C: A salesperson explains that the company's power washers are made of superior materials and have a lifetime guarantee.
options.D: A power washer has a sticker attached that says the machine performs heavy industrial cleaning.

questions.explanation: A salesperson states that if a power washer breaks within the first year of owning it, the company will repair or replace it. If a salesperson makes a promise—either verbally or in writing—that the company will repair or replace a defective product, s/he is making an express warranty. Television commercials advertising a power washer as the best heavy-duty cleaning device do not express any promises. A salesperson's statement that a device is made of superior materials or comes with a lifetime guarantee is not an express warranty. A power washer with a sticker attached detailing its heavy industrial cleaning use comes with an implied warranty; the sticker alludes to the kind of work that the machine can do.
questions.source: LAP-PM-004—Promises, Promises (Warranties and Guarantees)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain warranties and guarantees

questions.question: The ability to specialize in certain products and the ability to concentrate marketing efforts are two benefits of offering a __________ product mix.
questions.explanation: Narrow. A business with a narrow product mix offers a limited number of product lines. Having a narrow product mix allows a company to specialize effectively, produce efficiently, and concentrate its marketing efforts on its few product lines. Businesses with a broad product mix offer many product lines. Discount stores are good examples of businesses with broad product lines since they carry everything from shampoo to tires to books. If a business has many products in its product line(s), it has a long product mix. On the other hand, though, if a business doesn't have many items in its product line(s), it has a short product mix. Broad, short, and long product mixes do not offer the ability to specialize in certain products or to concentrate marketing efforts.
questions.source: LAP-PM-003—Mix and Match (The Nature of the Product Mix)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of product mix

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of product bundling:

options.A: A retail store holds a "buy one, get one 50% off" sale twice a season.
options.B: A restaurant discounts all of its salads and appetizers on Wednesday nights from 7-9 p.m.
options.C: A grocery store also has a bank, a florist, and a pharmacy inside its doors.
options.D: A company sells a computer, printer, and mouse together for a discounted price.

questions.explanation: A company sells a computer, printer, and mouse together for a discounted price. Product bundling is a marketing strategy that involves offering several products for sale as one combined product. Selling a computer, printer, and mouse together is an example of a product bundle. Discounts and other promotions such as “buy one get one 50% off” are also marketing tactics, but they are different from product bundling. A grocery store that offers other services is not an example of product bundling either.
questions.source: Leonard, K. (2018, October 23). Product bundling strategy. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/product-bundling-strategy-41789.html

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of product bundling
