questions.question: The Donut Hole is known for its unique donut creations with imaginative names. Despite the presence of competing bakeries, cafés, and donut shops, the Donut Hole is by far the most popular place for sweet treats in town. In other words, the Donut Hole has a
questions.explanation: Competitive advantage. A competitive advantage is any edge a company has that allows it to create more sales, generate more revenue, retain more customers, etc., than its competition. The Donut Hole in this example has a competitive advantage over other bakeries, cafés, and donut shops in the area because of its unique donut creations. The Donut Hole's popularity does not necessarily demonstrate its brand identity, corporate marketing strategy, or monopoly over the market.
questions.source: LAP-PM-019—Getting Piece of Mind (Factors Used To Position Products/Services)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe factors used by marketers to position products/services

questions.question: Tristan will only purchase Apple technology products, even if they are more expensive than the alternatives. In this instance, Apple has achieved brand
questions.explanation: Insistence. Brand insistence is the stage of brand loyalty in which consumers insist upon buying a specific brand. Tristan refuses to purchase any brand of technology products other than Apple, so Apple has achieved brand insistence. Brand recognition is the stage of brand loyalty in which consumers are made aware of a brand's existence. Brand preference is the stage of brand loyalty in which consumers prefer to purchase a certain brand but will accept substitutes if the brand is not available. Brand image includes impressions of a corporate brand within customers' minds which represent what the brand stands for.
questions.source: LAP-PM-006—It's a Brand, Brand, Brand World! (Nature of Product Branding)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of product/service branding

questions.question: Negative product reviews can be bad for business if a company does nothing to address its customers' dissatisfaction. If a company uses negative reviews to implement positive changes, however, negative feedback can actually be very helpful. This is an example of the importance of

options.A: using branding to prevent negative reviews.
options.B: hiring people to write fake reviews.

questions.explanation: Customer voice in branding. Customers' likes and dislikes should be taken into account when producing and branding a product or service. Products and services that are tailored to meet customers' wants and needs are much more likely to be successful than those that are not. This example demonstrates the importance of using all customer feedback to improve products and services, even if it is negative feedback. This example does not demonstrate the importance of hiring people to write fake reviews, deleting negative reviews, or using branding to prevent negative reviews.
questions.source: Minkara, O. (2015, March 30). The voice of the customer in branding: A simple formula for success. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://ww.aberdeen.com/cmo-essentials/the-voice-of-the-customer-in-branding-a-simple-formula-for-success/

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the role of customer voice in branding

questions.question: Ed's Quick Tires is committed to meeting its customers' automobile needs quickly and conveniently. This is the business's
questions.explanation: Brand promise. A brand promise is a business's spoken or unspoken agreement with customers that it will consistently meet their expectations and deliver on its brand characteristics and values. Making a commitment to meet customer needs quickly and conveniently is an example of a brand promise, not a brand identity, corporate brand, or brand values. A brand identity consists of those elements that are instantly recognized as representing a particular business or product. A corporate brand consists of all the combined customer impressions and experiences associated with a particular company. Brand values are beliefs or qualities that a corporate brand stands for and is built around.
questions.source: LAP-PM-020—Corporate Identity (Nature of Corporate Branding)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of corporate branding

questions.question: Ben is browsing the Internet when an advertisement for a car appears on his screen. Advertisements online are examples of brand
questions.explanation: Touchpoints. Touchpoints are all the opportunities that businesses have to connect with customers and reinforce their brand values. Any chance a business gets to interact with customers is a touchpoint; this includes products, packaging, employee interactions, websites, advertisements, social media interactions, and much more. Brand cues are simple reminders of a brand's identity and values, and are usually directed at employees. Brand values are beliefs or qualities that a corporate brand stands for and is built around. A brand promise is a business's spoken or unspoken agreement with customers that it will consistently meet their expectations and deliver on its brand characteristics and values.
questions.source: Uhlig, D.K. (2017, November 21). What is touchpoint marketing? Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/touchpoint-marketing-34078.html

performanceIndicator.text: Identify customer touch points

questions.question: Every time Gourmet Pet advertises for its dog food, it uses the same catchphrase: "The very best food for your very best friend." As a result, customers have come to associate Gourmet Pet's products with quality. This is an example of the importance of __________ in promotion.
questions.explanation: Repetition. The communication conveyed in promotions should be repeated over and over. Many customers would not remember the message if they heard it only once. Even the most memorable messages need to be repeated. Repetitive messages create sustained interest in products or ideas. Coordination, relevance, and appropriateness in promotion are also important, but these characteristics are not specifically demonstrated in this example.
questions.source: LAP-PR-002—Razzle Dazzle (Nature of Promotion)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of promotion as a marketing function

questions.question: Martin's Metalwork has too much stock in its inventory. Which promotional strategy is the most effective way to solve this issue?
questions.explanation: Sales promotion. Sales promotions, such as coupons, giveaways, or discounts, can help sell old stock or overstocked inventory by drawing customers to the merchandise in question. While publicity, advertising, and personal selling are all elements of the promotional mix, they are not as effective in solving the problem of too much inventory.
questions.source: LAP-PR-001—Spread the Word (Nature of the Promotional Mix)

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the elements of the promotional mix

questions.question: Customer distraction, low viewability rates, and high cost are all disadvantages of
questions.explanation: Online sales promotion. The Internet has ushered in an entire new world of technology-driven sales promotion. While there are many benefits of online promotion, there are also potential disadvantages such as customer distraction, low viewability, and high cost. Traditional print ads and in-store sales promotions are generally cheaper, hold a more captive audience, and have higher viewability rates than online sales promotions. Promotional sponsorships, such as partnerships with celebrities or other businesses, may also be costly but may be more effective in capturing customer attention.
questions.source: Brookins, M. (2018, June 29). Disadvantages of online advertising options. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/disadvantages-online-advertising-options-10212.html

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in the promotion function

questions.question: Which of the following promotional efforts is most likely to be illegal:

options.A: A car commercial exaggerates its vehicles' horsepower.
options.B: A fast-food restaurant's ad claims its salads are healthy.
options.C: A makeup commercial includes airbrushed models.
options.D: A department store says it will match any competitor's price.

questions.explanation: A car commercial exaggerates its vehicles' horsepower. It is illegal to make misleading and/or false claims about products. If a car company is exaggerating its vehicles' horsepower in its advertisements, it is likely breaking the law. “Healthy” is a subjective term, so a fast-food restaurant likely would not get in trouble for claiming its salads are healthy. Airbrushed models are common in advertisements; alone, this practice would not cause legal trouble for the makeup commercial. Price matching is also a common competitive technique and is not illegal.
questions.source: Federal Trade Commission. (2015, June 15). Truth in advertising. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/media-resources/truth-advertising

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the regulation of promotion

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of advertising on network television:
questions.explanation: Reach. Advertisements on network television can reach a very broad audience because anyone can watch network television. However, they can also be extremely expensive. Network television ads are not meant for a highly specific audience; rather, a cable or local TV ad could reach a more targeted group of people. Finally, it is not easy to create and produce a network television advertisement.
questions.source: LAP-PR-003—Ad-quipping Your Business (Types of Advertising Media)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of advertising media

questions.question: Jamie is a loyal customer of Glamor Girl cosmetics. She purchases every new product the company releases, writes glowing reviews online, and tells her friends and family to try the brand's cosmetics. Jamie could be described as a
questions.explanation: Brand evangelist. Brand evangelists are loyal customers that act as unofficial brand ambassadors to their friends and family members by recommending and endorsing the brand's products. In this example, Jamie could be described as a brand evangelist—not a late adopter, potential customer, or discount customer. A late adopter is someone who is skeptical of a new product and therefore slow to begin using or buying that good or service. A potential customer is someone with a particular want or need who is highly likely to purchase your product. A discount customer is someone that makes purchasing decisions based on the size of current markdowns.
questions.source: Clark, D. (2012, January 28). How to turn your customers into evangelists. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.forbes.com/sites/dorieclark/2012/01/28/how-to-turn-your-customers-into-evangelists/#286dba031ded

performanceIndicator.text: Describe word-of-mouth channels used to communicate with targeted audiences

questions.question: Nelly recently purchased a new toaster oven. The manufacturer of the toaster offered a special promotion where Nelly could receive $50 cash back if she mailed her proof-of-purchase to the company. This is known as a
questions.explanation: Rebate. A rebate is a sales promotion in which part of the price a customer pays for a good is given back to the customer. Usually rebates require customers to mail proof-of-purchase to receive their money back. This example does not demonstrate a point-of-sale promotion, coupon, or sweepstakes. Point-of-sale promotions are promotions located where the customer purchases a good or service, such as in a store. A coupon is a printed or online certificate that entitles the holder to a reduced purchase price. A sweepstakes is a game of chance in which a customer wins a prize.
questions.source: Inc.com. (2018, May 17). Rebates. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.inc.com/encyclopedia/rebates.html

performanceIndicator.text: Identify communications channels used in sales promotion

questions.question: Oliver is leafing through a magazine when he comes across an advertisement for a sports drink that catches his eye. In bold text, the ad says “More Power for Your Performance.” This text is the advertisement's
questions.explanation: Headline. An ad's headline provides short, memorable text that gives readers an idea of what the ad is about. “More Power for Your Performance” is an example of a headline because it is short, eye-catching, and provides a brief explanation of the product's benefit. A call to action is text that provides specific instructions to customers such as “call now to reserve your copy.” The body of the advertisement includes details about the product or service and any other important information. White space is the space between the advertisement's components that gives the advertisement a clean, professional appearance.
questions.source: Erickson, A. (2017, November 21). 7 elements of print advertising. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://yourbusiness.azcentral.com/7-elements-print-advertising-5911.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the components of advertisements

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding white space in advertisements is true:

options.A: White space is a waste of valuable advertising space that could be filled with text.
options.B: People usually spend more time reading advertisements with no white space.
options.C: White space can be used to keep readers engaged with the advertisement.
options.D: Advertisements with very little white space are generally more successful.

questions.explanation: White space can be used to keep readers engaged with the advertisement. White space is blank space in a print advertisement that is unoccupied by text or pictures. White space is an important design tool that is used to keep readers engaged and to prevent reader fatigue. People usually spend much more time reading ads that have adequate white space than ads with not enough; therefore, white space is not a waste of space but a valuable component of any advertisement. Ads with very little white space are unlikely to hold readers' attention and so will not be successful.
questions.source: Soegaard, M. (2018). The power of white space. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.interaction-design.org/literature/article/the-power-of-white-space

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the importance of coordinating elements in advertisements

questions.question: Sari's restaurant is hosting a family fun night with food specials, carnival games, and face painting. She wants to get the word out about the event to the general public, but she's not sure how. Which of the following public relations tools would be most appropriate:
questions.explanation: Press release. A press release is written information provided to the media to obtain publicity about something, oftentimes an event or other noteworthy occurrence. A press release to local news media would be an easy and effective way for Sari to get the basic information about the event out to the public. An email to current customers or a newsletter might inform customers about the event, but they would not inform the general public. A press conference would be inappropriate for this situation; press conferences are generally reserved for major announcements or developments.
questions.source: Wynne, R. (2016, June 13). How to write a press release. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.forbes.com/sites/robertwynne/2016/06/13/how-to-write-a-press-release/#3054ef613b93

performanceIndicator.text: Identify types of public-relations activities

questions.question: Public relations efforts aimed at a company's own employees are often attempting to

options.A: educate the public about the company.

questions.explanation: Maintain employee goodwill. Public relations efforts that are aimed at employees are often attempts to enhance employee morale and maintain employee goodwill toward the business. Educating the public about the company is the purpose of other types of public relations, such as those that are aimed at consumers. Taking advantage of employees is not usually a purpose of public relations. Selling products and services is an indirect goal of public relations aimed at the public, but it is not the ultimate purpose.
questions.source: Advameg, Inc. (2019). Public relations. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from http://www.referenceforbusiness.com/small/Op-Qu/Public-Relations.html

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss internal and external audiences for public-relations activities

questions.question: A salesperson can provide excellent customer service before a customer even makes a purchase by

options.A: discussing follow-up care for the product.
options.B: ensuring that shipping is done correctly.

questions.explanation: Using suggestion selling. Suggestion selling is a sales technique in which the salesperson attempts to increase the customer's purchase by recommending additional items after the original decision to buy has been made. Salespeople can provide excellent customer service before a sale has been made by using suggestion selling and helping customers decide which products to buy. Ensuring that shipping is done correctly, discussing follow-up care for the product, and offering technical assistance are all ways of providing customer service after a sale has been made.
questions.source: LAP-SE-130—Go Beyond the Sale (Customer Service in Selling)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships

questions.question: Andy, a car salesman, has worked hard to build strong relationships with his clients. As a result of his efforts, many of his customers return to his dealership each time they purchase a new car. This example demonstrates how building a clientele can

options.B: lead to more work for salespeople.

questions.explanation: Increase customer loyalty. Loyal customers return to buy on a regular basis. They are the financial backbone for any business. Because they continue to buy from the business, their support often leads to an increase in sales volume and reduced selling costs, not fewer overall sales. Maintaining strong relationships with customers is always hard work, but maintaining current relationships is less work than trying to establish new ones.
questions.source: LAP-SE-115—Keep Them Loyal (Key Factors in Building Clientele)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain key factors in building a clientele

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding company selling policies is true:

options.A: Companies with large sales forces usually operate without written sales policies and instead rely on the policies being passed on verbally.
options.B: Salespeople very rarely adhere to company selling policies because they are too rigid and limit the sales process.
options.C: Selling policies are very useful in routine selling situations because they outline how the sales process should go.
options.D: Companies with small sales forces usually operate using formal, written sales policies rather than relying on the policies being passed on verbally.

questions.explanation: Selling policies are very useful in routine selling situations because they outline how the sales process should go. Selling policies are the general rules that a business's leaders set to guide the personal-selling effort. Selling policies are very useful in routine selling situations because they outline how the selling process should go and ensure that all customers are treated fairly and consistently. Good salespeople always adhere to company selling policies because they ensure that customers are treated fairly and consistently. When it comes to implementing selling policies, companies with large sales forces often operate differently than companies with small sales forces. Companies with large sales forces usually provide policy handbooks that fully explain all selling policies to sales trainees. On the other hand, small companies with few salespeople may operate without written policies and may rely on policies being passed on verbally.
questions.source: LAP-SE-932—Sell Right (Selling Policies)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain company selling policies

questions.question: A technology store recently ran an advertisement for a discounted laptop computer. However, when Allison visited the store looking for the laptop, the salesperson tried to sell her a much more expensive model instead. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Bait-and-switch advertising. Bait-and-switch advertising involves promoting a low-priced item to attract customers to whom the business then tries to sell a higher priced item. Bait-and-switch advertising is illegal under U.S. law and in many other countries. Deceptive pricing involves advertising a product for a certain price and then selling it for a more expensive price. Referral selling typically involves offering incentives or prizes to customers in exchange for providing the names of other potential customers to the company (receiving the incentive is usually contingent on the other customer making a purchase). Dry testing a product refers to “testing out” the desirability of a certain product by advertising for it before it has actually been produced. Deceptive pricing, referral selling, and dry testing are also illegal selling practices, but they are not demonstrated in this example.
questions.source: Nicolosi, P. (2018). 6 online deceptive pricing & sales practices to avoid! Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.internetlegalattorney.com/6-online-deceptive-pricing-sales-practices-to-avoid/

questions.question: Marty is a kitchen appliance salesperson. When a customer looking for a refrigerator is having trouble deciding which model to buy, Marty describes each product's unique features and benefits. As a result, the customer is able to decide which refrigerator to purchase. Marty is a successful salesperson because he

options.A: is enthusiastic about the products he sells.
options.B: offers as few products as possible for customers to choose from.
options.C: gives vague, ambiguous answers to customer questions.
options.D: is knowledgeable about the products he sells.

questions.explanation: Is knowledgeable about the products he sells. Having appropriate product information benefits a salesperson by boosting enthusiasm, increasing confidence and credibility, ensuring accuracy in sales presentations, helping overcome customer objections, and increasing sales. Salespeople should know important information, such as how a product was made, how a product should be used, what discounts are available, etc. In this example, Marty's extensive knowledge about the refrigerators offered by his store led his customer to make a purchase that was right for her. This example does not demonstrate the importance of being enthusiastic about the products you sell. Salespeople should offer multiple options for customers to choose from and provide clear, concrete answers to customer questions.
questions.source: LAP-SE-131—Get Informed (Acquiring Product Information for Use in Selling)

performanceIndicator.text: Acquire product information for use in selling

questions.question: Krista works at a pool supply store. One of the products she sells is a waterproof speaker system. The speaker system is popular because customers don't have to worry about getting it wet when they are using it by the pool. The ability to get the speakers wet is a(n) __________ benefit.
questions.explanation: Obvious. Obvious or apparent benefits are advantages that need little explanation by the salesperson. The customer already knows, or can easily recognize, the benefit. A speaker system that is waterproof has the obvious benefit of being able to get wet, and salespeople do not necessarily need to inform customers of this benefit. Unique or exclusive benefits are advantages that are available only from your good, service, or business. Krista's waterproof speakers are probably not the only speakers that are waterproof, so this example does not demonstrate an exclusive benefit. Hidden benefits are advantages that cannot be seen or understood without the assistance of a salesperson. In this example, the benefit of waterproof speakers is clear and easily understood. "Unfamiliar" is not a term generally used to describe types of product benefits.
questions.source: LAP-SE-113—Find Features, Boost Benefits (Feature-Benefit Selling)

performanceIndicator.text: Analyze product information to identify product features and benefits

questions.question: Which of the following customers would be considered a qualified prospect for a luxury sailboat company:

options.A: A college student on his university's sailing team
options.B: A middle-aged parent who enjoys kayaking on vacation
options.C: A wealthy retiree with a summer house on the bay
options.D: A busy young professional with a passion for water sports

questions.explanation: A wealthy retiree with a summer house on the bay. A qualified prospect is a potential customer who is likely to have a need or want for a specific product, as well as the ability to pay for the product. In this case, the only customer qualified for a luxury sailboat would most likely be the wealthy retiree with a summer house on the water. This customer is both retired and wealthy, meaning s/he probably has plenty of time to enjoy a luxury sailboat—as well as the money to afford one. S/He also has a house located on a body of water, making him/her more likely to be interested in a sailboat than a customer with no house on the water. A middle-aged parent who enjoys kayaking is probably not qualified to buy a luxury sailboat because of the responsibilities and budget constraints involved with raising a family. A college student on his university's sailing team is most likely unable to afford a luxury sailboat at his age. A busy young professional with a passion for water sports is probably too involved in his/her career, relationships, or extracurricular involvements to have time for a sailboat, and may not be able to afford one.
questions.source: LAP-SE-048—Set Your Sales (The Selling Process)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the selling process

questions.question: Laurie recently purchased and installed a new smoke detector in her home. Laurie's purchase most likely fulfilled which of the following needs within Maslow's Hierarchy:
questions.explanation: Safety. Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs is a motivational theory that categorizes human needs into levels that help explain how and why people are motivated. One of the most basic levels of needs within the hierarchy is safety. Laurie's purchase of a smoke detector indicates that she was attempting to satisfy her need for safety and security. Esteem needs include the needs for feelings of accomplishment and prestige. Physiological needs are the needs for food, water, warmth, and rest. Self-actualization refers to achieving one's full potential in life.
questions.source: McLeod, S. (2018). Maslow's hierarchy of needs. Retrieved January 10, 2019, from https://www.simplypsychology.org/maslow.html

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss motivational theories that impact buying behavior
